/* D3D9 shader bytecode -> WGSL: the WebGPU twin of vs_to_msl / ps_to_msl_ex2.
 *
 * Included at the end of vsemu.c (wasm builds, or native with -DVSEMU_WGSL for
 * offline tools) so it shares the parser's private VSProg/VSIns and token
 * macros.  Its contract with the renderer:
 * module layout, bindings, structs, override constants.
 *
 * Semantics are the Mac backends' on purpose (the Mac build is the reference
 * look), instruction for instruction: same register masking, same defaults,
 * same edge cases (rcp/rsq/log of 0), same skipped ps_1_x texture ops, same
 * ps_2_0 t# quirk (behind an opt-in override).  Where WGSL forces a different
 * spelling the comment says so:
 *   - no masked swizzle assignment: writes are expanded per component;
 *   - no implicit float->int: a0 writes convert explicitly (truncation, as the
 *     MSL implicit conversion; mova rounds half away from zero, as MSL round);
 *   - constant expressions that overflow (1.0/0.0, log2(0.0) ...) are shader
 *     creation errors, so `def` constants are function-scope `let`s and every
 *     register read is a runtime value: nothing can ever be const-folded into
 *     an error;
 *   - no preprocessor: the MSL macros (SMPk, TSEL, LDF ...) become helpers.
 * Every module is complete text (no prelude added by the renderer) with one
 * entry point. */
#include <stdarg.h>
#include "wgsl.h"
#include "gpu_proto.h"
#define WSTR_(x) #x
#define WSTR(x) WSTR_(x)

typedef struct { char *p; size_t cap, n; int ok; } WBuf;
static void wb_init(WBuf *b, char *p, size_t cap){
    b->p = p; b->cap = cap; b->n = 0; b->ok = (p && cap > 0);
    if (b->ok) p[0] = 0;
}
static void wb_put(WBuf *b, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
static void wb_put(WBuf *b, const char *fmt, ...){
    if (!b->ok) return;
    va_list ap; va_start(ap, fmt);
    int w = vsnprintf(b->p + b->n, b->cap - b->n, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
    if (w < 0 || (size_t)w >= b->cap - b->n){ b->ok = 0; b->p[b->n] = 0; return; }
    b->n += (size_t)w;
}

/* ---- shared module text ---- */
static const char W_VOUT[] =
    "struct VOut {\n"
    "  @builtin(position) pos: vec4f,\n"
    "  @location(0) col0: vec4f, @location(1) col1: vec4f,\n"
    "  @location(2) uv0: vec4f, @location(3) uv1: vec4f, @location(4) uv2: vec4f, @location(5) uv3: vec4f,\n"
    "  @location(6) fog: f32,\n"
    "}\n";
/* K is a 64 KB window of the frame's VS constant arena, bound once for many
 * draws; a draw's block {stride, tsel, base, target w | h << 16; c[0..255]} starts at row
 * kb = instance_index (the draw's firstInstance), so a draw no longer needs a
 * bind group of its own. */
static const char W_VSPAR[] =
    "struct VSWin { c: array<vec4f, " WSTR(GW_KWIN_ROWS) "> }\n"
    "@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> VB: array<u32>;\n"
    "@group(0) @binding(1) var<uniform> K: VSWin;\n";
/* Byte-addressed little-endian loads from the vertex buffer at any alignment
 * (a misaligned u32 combines two words).  The same text is used by the pull
 * test module, so the compute test checks exactly what the VS modules run. */
static const char W_PULL[] =
    "fn ld32(a: u32) -> u32 {\n"
    "  let w = a >> 2u;\n"
    "  let s = (a & 3u) << 3u;\n"
    "  if (s == 0u) { return VB[w]; }\n"
    "  return (VB[w] >> s) | (VB[w + 1u] << (32u - s));\n"
    "}\n"
    "fn ld16(a: u32) -> u32 {\n"
    "  let s = (a & 3u) << 3u;\n"
    "  if (s <= 16u) { return (VB[a >> 2u] >> s) & 0xFFFFu; }\n"
    "  return ld32(a) & 0xFFFFu;\n"
    "}\n"
    "fn ldf(a: u32) -> f32 { return bitcast<f32>(ld32(a)); }\n"
    "fn lds(a: u32) -> f32 { return f32(bitcast<i32>(ld16(a) << 16u) >> 16u); }\n"
    "fn ldu(a: u32) -> f32 { return f32(ld16(a)); }\n"
    "fn ldub4(a: u32) -> vec4f {\n"
    "  let u = ld32(a);\n"
    "  return vec4f(f32(u & 0xFFu), f32((u >> 8u) & 0xFFu), f32((u >> 16u) & 0xFFu), f32(u >> 24u));\n"
    "}\n"
    /* x / y rounded exactly like the C division in decl_fetch: the
     * reciprocal product corrected by one FMA residual step (r = f32(1/y)).
     * A plain WGSL division is not correctly rounded on the GPU (measured in
     * Chrome on Metal: 126 of the 256 byte values of b/255 differ by 1 ulp);
     * this form matched all 256 + 65536 + 65536 cases of /255, /32767, /65535. */
    "fn cdiv(x: vec4f, y: f32, r: f32) -> vec4f {\n"
    "  let q = x * r;\n"
    "  return fma(fma(-q, vec4f(y), x), vec4f(r), q);\n"
    "}\n"
    "fn n8(x: vec4f) -> vec4f { return cdiv(x, 255.0, 0x1.010102p-8); }\n"
    "fn s16n(x: vec4f) -> vec4f { return cdiv(x, 32767.0, 0x1.0002p-15); }\n"
    "fn u16n(x: vec4f) -> vec4f { return cdiv(x, 65535.0, 0x1.0001p-16); }\n"
    "fn ldcolor(a: u32) -> vec4f { return n8(ldub4(a).zyxw); }\n";
static const char W_TPICK[] =
    "fn tpick(s: u32, a: vec4f, b: vec4f, c: vec4f, d: vec4f) -> vec4f {\n"
    "  return select(select(a, b, s == 1u), select(c, d, s == 3u), s >= 2u);\n"
    "}\n";
static const char W_PSPAR[] =
    "struct PSPar { aref: f32, usec: f32, pad0: f32, pad1: f32, proj: vec4f, c: array<vec4f, 32>, fog: vec4f }\n"
    "@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> P: PSPar;\n"
    "override ALPHA_FUNC: u32 = 7u;\n"
    "override PS20_TEXCOORD: bool = true;\n"
    /* D3DCMP against P.aref; 7 is spelled !(a < r) so a NaN alpha passes, as
     * the Mac's "if (a < aref) discard" does. */
    "fn alpha_pass(a: f32, r: f32) -> bool {\n"
    "  switch ALPHA_FUNC {\n"
    "    case 1u: { return false; }\n"
    "    case 2u: { return a < r; }\n"
    "    case 3u: { return a == r; }\n"
    "    case 4u: { return a <= r; }\n"
    "    case 5u: { return a > r; }\n"
    "    case 6u: { return a != r; }\n"
    "    case 7u: { return !(a < r); }\n"
    "    default: { return true; }\n"
    "  }\n"
    "}\n"
    /* Alpha test, then D3D9 vertex fog C = f*Cs + (1-f)*Cfog on rgb only;
     * P.fog.a = FOGENABLE.  ALPHA_FUNC 8 folds the discard away (the Mac's
     * no-discard twin, which keeps hidden-surface removal on Apple GPUs). */
    "fn ps_end(c: vec4f, fog: f32) -> vec4f {\n"
    "  if (ALPHA_FUNC != 8u) { if (!alpha_pass(c.a, P.aref)) { discard; } }\n"
    "  return vec4f(mix(P.fog.rgb, c.rgb, mix(1.0, saturate(fog), P.fog.a)), c.a);\n"
    "}\n"
    /* ps_1_x coordinate of stage k: P.proj[k] = coordIndex + 16*projMode,
     * mode 1 divides by z, 2 by w (texproj_push in com.c).  select(), not a
     * branch, keeps the sample in uniform control flow. */
    "fn tcoord(q: vec4f, sel: f32) -> vec2f {\n"
    "  let m = i32(sel) >> 4u;\n"
    "  return q.xy / select(select(1.0, q.z, m == 1), q.w, m == 2);\n"
    "}\n";

static void w_textures(WBuf *b, unsigned cubemask){
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++)
        wb_put(b, "@group(1) @binding(%d) var tex%d: %s;\n", k, k,
               ((cubemask >> k) & 1u) ? "texture_cube<f32>" : "texture_2d<f32>");
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++)
        wb_put(b, "@group(1) @binding(%d) var smp%d: sampler;\n", 4 + k, k);
}

/* f32 literal that survives a round trip (9 significant digits) and always
 * reads as a float.  Non-finite values have no WGSL literal: reject (the Mac's
 * %g would print "inf"/"nan", which does not compile in MSL either). */
static int w_float(char *o, size_t cap, float f){
    if (!isfinite(f)) return 0;
    char t[48]; snprintf(t, sizeof t, "%.9g", (double)f);
    if (!strpbrk(t, ".e")) snprintf(o, cap, "%s.0", t);
    else snprintf(o, cap, "%s", t);
    return 1;
}

/* ---- register naming (msl_reg with WGSL names) ---- */
typedef struct {
    const VSProg *p;
    int      vs;            /* 1 = vertex shader (K.c, r0..r31, v0..v15, a0) */
    uint32_t r, v, t, ci;   /* registers used (bit n) */
    uint32_t cdef[8];       /* def'd constants used */
    int      a0, aL, oC, Z, dummy;
    int      bad;           /* text overflow or unsupported operand: reject */
} WCtx;

static void w_reg(WCtx *x, char *o, size_t cap, unsigned tok, unsigned rel){
    const VSProg *p = x->p;
    int ty = RT(tok), n = RN(tok), vs = x->vs;
    switch (ty){
    case R_TEMP:  n &= vs ? 31 : 15; x->r |= 1u << n; snprintf(o, cap, "r%d", n); return;
    case R_INPUT: n &= vs ? 15 : 1;  x->v |= 1u << n; snprintf(o, cap, "v%d", n); return;
    case R_ADDR:
        if (vs){ x->a0 = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "vec4f(a0)"); }
        else   { n &= 3; x->t |= 1u << n; snprintf(o, cap, "t%d", n); }
        return;
    case R_LOOP:     x->aL = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "vec4f(f32(aL))"); return;
    case R_COLOROUT: x->oC = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "oC"); return;
    case R_CONSTINT:
        if (n >= 0 && n < 16){ x->ci |= 1u << n; snprintf(o, cap, "i%d", n); }
        else { x->Z = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "Z"); }
        return;
    case R_CONST: case R_CONST2: case R_CONST3: case R_CONST4: {
        int idx = n;
        if (ty == R_CONST2) idx += 2048; else if (ty == R_CONST3) idx += 4096;
        else if (ty == R_CONST4) idx += 6144;
        /* relative addressing (vertex only, as on the Mac): c[a0.<comp> + idx],
         * clamped to the 256-entry array */
        if (RELADDR(tok) && vs){
            char comp = 'x';
            if (rel){
                if (RT(rel) == R_LOOP) comp = 0;
                else comp = SWCH[SWIZ(rel) & 3u];
            }
            if (comp){ x->a0 = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "K.c[kb + 1u + u32(clamp(a0.%c + %d, 0, 255))]", comp, idx); }
            else     { x->aL = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "K.c[kb + 1u + u32(clamp(aL + %d, 0, 255))]", idx); }
            return;
        }
        if (idx >= 0 && idx < 256 && (p->defmask[idx >> 5] & (1u << (idx & 31)))){
            x->cdef[idx >> 5] |= 1u << (idx & 31);
            snprintf(o, cap, "c%d", idx);
        } else if (vs) snprintf(o, cap, "K.c[kb + %du]", (idx & 255) + 1);   /* row 0 of the block is its header */
        else snprintf(o, cap, "P.c[%d]", idx & 31);
        return; }
    default: x->Z = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "Z"); return;
    }
}

/* Source operand: register + swizzle + source modifier (msl_src). */
static void w_src(WCtx *x, char *o, size_t cap, unsigned tok, unsigned rel){
    char reg[96]; w_reg(x, reg, sizeof reg, tok, rel);
    unsigned sw = SWIZ(tok);
    char sws[8];
    if (sw == 0xE4u) sws[0] = 0;
    else { sws[0] = '.'; for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) sws[1+i] = SWCH[(sw >> (2*i)) & 3u]; sws[5] = 0; }
    char body[128];
    snprintf(body, sizeof body, "%s%s", reg, sws);
    int w;
    switch (SMOD(tok)){
    case 1:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(-%s)", body); break;                    /* NEG  */
    case 2:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(%s - 0.5)", body); break;               /* BIAS */
    case 3:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(-(%s - 0.5))", body); break;
    case 4:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(2.0 * %s - 1.0)", body); break;         /* SIGN (bx2) */
    case 5:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(-(2.0 * %s - 1.0))", body); break;
    case 6:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(1.0 - %s)", body); break;               /* COMP */
    case 7:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(2.0 * %s)", body); break;               /* X2   */
    case 8:  w = snprintf(o, cap, "(-2.0 * %s)", body); break;
    case 11: w = snprintf(o, cap, "abs(%s)", body); break;                  /* ABS  */
    case 12: w = snprintf(o, cap, "(-abs(%s))", body); break;
    default: w = snprintf(o, cap, "%s", body); break;
    }
    if (w < 0 || (size_t)w >= cap) x->bad = 1;
}

/* Write `val` (a vec4f expression) to `name` under the destination's write
 * mask.  WGSL has no masked swizzle assignment, so a partial mask evaluates
 * once into a let and stores component by component.  `toint` converts for
 * the integer destination a0 (truncation toward zero, as MSL's implicit
 * float -> int conversion). */
static void w_store(WBuf *b, const char *name, unsigned mask, const char *val, int toint){
    if (mask == 0u || mask == 0xFu){
        if (toint) wb_put(b, "  %s = vec4i(%s);\n", name, val);
        else       wb_put(b, "  %s = %s;\n", name, val);
        return;
    }
    wb_put(b, "  { let e = %s;", val);
    for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++)
        if (mask & (1u << c)){
            if (toint) wb_put(b, " %s.%c = i32(e.%c);", name, SWCH[c], SWCH[c]);
            else       wb_put(b, " %s.%c = e.%c;", name, SWCH[c], SWCH[c]);
        }
    wb_put(b, " }\n");
}

static void w_decls(WBuf *b, const WCtx *x, int nr){
    if (x->Z) wb_put(b, "  let Z = vec4f(0.0);\n");
    for (int i = 0; i < nr; i++) if (x->r & (1u << i)) wb_put(b, "  var r%d = vec4f(0.0);\n", i);
    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++){
        if (!(x->cdef[i >> 5] & (1u << (i & 31)))) continue;
        char f[4][48];
        for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) w_float(f[c], sizeof f[c], x->p->def[i][c]);
        wb_put(b, "  let c%d = vec4f(%s, %s, %s, %s);\n", i, f[0], f[1], f[2], f[3]);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) if (x->ci & (1u << i))
        wb_put(b, "  let i%d = vec4f(%d.0, %d.0, %d.0, %d.0);\n", i, x->p->defi[i][0],
               x->p->defi[i][1], x->p->defi[i][2], x->p->defi[i][3]);
    if (x->a0) wb_put(b, "  var a0 = vec4i(0);\n");
    if (x->aL) wb_put(b, "  var aL: i32 = 0;\n");
    if (x->dummy) wb_put(b, "  var dummy = vec4f(0.0);\n");
}

static int w_defs_finite(const VSProg *p){
    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
        if (p->defmask[i >> 5] & (1u << (i & 31)))
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) if (!isfinite(p->def[i][c])) return 0;
    return 1;
}

/* The other cars' headlights (runtime/headlights.c, gpu_proto.h GwHL).  The
 * worldheadlight pixel shaders (ps_1_1) light a surface with
 *     mul rA.rgb, t1, t2          headlight texture (stage 1, at uv1.xy / uv1.w)
 *                                 x falloff ramp (stage 2)
 *     mad rA.rgb, rA, c0, v0      x HEADLIGHTCOLOR + the vertex light
 * before the texture multiply; after that mad, every other car's light is
 * added the same way, from its coordinate uv1 * t and its own colour.  p.z
 * is not the projector's depth but the point's height above that car's road
 * plane (metres): the light fades out from 2 m + 6 % of the distance ahead
 * (p.w) below it, gone 1.5 m lower, so a car on an overpass does not light
 * the street under it. */
static const char W_HL[] =
    "struct HLight { t: mat4x4f, col: vec4f }\n"
    "struct HLPar { n: u32, s: f32, o: f32, pad: f32, l: array<HLight, " WSTR(GW_HL_MAX) "> }\n"
    "@group(0) @binding(3) var<uniform> H: HLPar;\n"
    "fn hl_more(q: vec4f, v: f32) -> vec3f {\n"
    "  var a = vec3f(0.0);\n"
    "  for (var k = 0u; k < min(H.n, " WSTR(GW_HL_MAX) "u); k++) {\n"
    "    let p = q * H.l[k].t;\n"
    "    let l1 = textureSample(tex1, smp1, p.xy / p.w).rgb;\n"
    "    let l2 = textureSample(tex2, smp2, vec2f(H.s * p.w + H.o, v)).rgb;\n"
    "    let road = saturate((p.z + 3.5 + 0.06 * p.w) / 1.5);\n"
    "    a += select(vec3f(0.0), l1 * l2 * H.l[k].col.rgb * road, p.w > 0.0);\n"
    "  }\n"
    "  return a;\n"
    "}\n";
static int w_plain(unsigned tok, int ty, int n){
    return RT(tok) == ty && RN(tok) == n && SWIZ(tok) == 0xE4u && SMOD(tok) == 0;
}

/* ====================================================================
 * Pixel shader (ps_to_msl_ex2)
 * ==================================================================== */
#define WEX 4096
int ps_to_wgsl_ex2(const VSProg *p, int id, char *out, size_t cap, unsigned cubemask, int reflk){
    if (!p || !out || cap < 512) return 0;
    if (reflk >= 0) return 0;                   /* HD reflection variants: Mac-only */
    if (!w_defs_finite(p)) return 0;
    WCtx x; memset(&x, 0, sizeof x); x.p = p; x.vs = 0;
    char *bodybuf = malloc(cap);
    if (!bodybuf) return 0;
    WBuf bb; wb_init(&bb, bodybuf, cap);
    char *ex = malloc(WEX), *s0 = malloc(WEX), *s1 = malloc(WEX), *s2 = malloc(WEX), *val = malloc(WEX);
    int rc = 0;
    if (!ex || !s0 || !s1 || !s2 || !val) goto done;

    /* ps_2_0: `dcl tN` coordinate registers, loaded as D3D does.  The Mac
     * never loads them (they read 0, gfx-d3d9.md section 9 #1): then depth
     * of field (the scenes before and after a race) samples one texel and
     * leaves only the light glows on a flat colour.  PS20_TEXCOORD = false
     * gives the Mac's look (A/B). */
    if (p->version >= 0x0200){
        for (unsigned q = 0; q < p->n; q++){
            const VSIns *y = &p->ins[q];
            if (y->op != O_DCL || RT(y->dst) != R_ADDR) continue;
            int k = RN(y->dst) & 3;
            x.t |= 1u << k;
            wb_put(&bb, "  t%d = select(vec4f(0.0), i.uv%d, PS20_TEXCOORD);\n", k, k);
        }
    }
    /* Coordinates only for stages that are sampled through tex / texld tM
     * (same rule as the Mac: tcuse). */
    unsigned tcuse = 0;
    for (unsigned q = 0; q < p->n; q++){
        const VSIns *y = &p->ins[q];
        if (y->op != O_TEX && y->op != O_TEXLDD && y->op != O_TEXLDL) continue;
        if (y->nsrc == 1 && RT(y->src[0]) == R_ADDR) tcuse |= 1u << (RN(y->src[0]) & 3);
        else if (y->nsrc == 0)                       tcuse |= 1u << (RN(y->dst) & 3);
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++)
        if (tcuse & (1u << k)) wb_put(&bb, "  let tc%d = tcoord(i.uv%d, P.proj[%d]);\n", k, k, k);

    int hl_mul = -1, hl_used = 0;
    for (unsigned q = 0; q < p->n && bb.ok && !x.bad; q++){
        const VSIns *y = &p->ins[q];
        if (y->nsrc > 0) w_src(&x, s0, WEX, y->src[0], y->rel[0]);
        if (y->nsrc > 1) w_src(&x, s1, WEX, y->src[1], y->rel[1]);
        if (y->nsrc > 2) w_src(&x, s2, WEX, y->src[2], y->rel[2]);
        int w = 0;
        ex[0] = 0;
        switch (y->op){
        case O_NOP: case O_DCL: case O_DEF: case O_DEFI: case O_DEFB:
        case O_LABEL: case O_END:
            continue;
        case O_TEX: case O_TEXLDD: case O_TEXLDL: {
            /* ps_1_x "tex tN": sampler N, coordinate N (projective)
             * ps_1_4 "texld rN, tM": sampler N, coordinate M
             * ps_1_4 "texld rN, rM": dependent read at rM.xy
             * ps_2_0 "texld d, src, sN": sampler N at src.xy
             * A cube stage samples the 3-component vector (no divide). */
            int dn = RN(y->dst) & 3, smp, crd = -1;
            const char *cs = 0;
            if (y->nsrc >= 2){ smp = RN(y->src[1]) & 3; cs = s0; }
            else if (y->nsrc == 1 && RT(y->src[0]) == R_ADDR){ smp = dn; crd = RN(y->src[0]) & 3; }
            else if (y->nsrc == 1){ smp = dn; cs = s0; }
            else { smp = dn; crd = dn; }
            int cube = (cubemask >> smp) & 1u;
            if (crd >= 0){
                if (cube) w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "textureSample(tex%d, smp%d, i.uv%d.xyz)", smp, smp, crd);
                else      w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "textureSample(tex%d, smp%d, tc%d)", smp, smp, crd);
            } else {
                w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "textureSample(tex%d, smp%d, (%s).%s)", smp, smp, cs, cube ? "xyz" : "xy");
            }
            break; }
        case O_TEXCOORD: {
            /* texcoord tN / texcrd: t[N] = uvN (the Mac uses the destination
             * number for both, also for ps_1_4 texcrd rN, tM) */
            int dn = RN(y->dst) & 3;
            x.t |= 1u << dn;
            wb_put(&bb, "  t%d = i.uv%d;\n", dn, dn);
            continue; }
        case O_TEXKILL: {
            /* texkill's register is its destination token (no sources).
             * D3D9: ps_1_x tests the first three components of texture
             * coordinate set N (texkill tN) or, ps_1_4, of a temp (rN);
             * ps_2_0 and later all four components of the register (as
             * Wine's shader_glsl_texkill).  The Mac's MSL reads the unset
             * source operand instead (vsemu.c), a bug not carried over;
             * NFSU2's shaders have no texkill. */
            int kty = RT(y->dst);
            char kr[64];
            if (kty == R_ADDR && p->version < 0x0200) snprintf(kr, sizeof kr, "i.uv%d", RN(y->dst) & 3);
            else if (kty == R_TEMP || kty == R_ADDR) w_reg(&x, kr, sizeof kr, y->dst, 0);
            else { x.bad = 1; continue; }
            if (p->version >= 0x0200) wb_put(&bb, "  if (any(%s < vec4f(0.0))) { discard; }\n", kr);
            else                      wb_put(&bb, "  if (any(%s.xyz < vec3f(0.0))) { discard; }\n", kr);
            continue; }
        case O_MOV:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "%s", s0); break;
        case O_ADD:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) + (%s)", s0, s1); break;
        case O_SUB:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) - (%s)", s0, s1); break;
        case O_MUL:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) * (%s)", s0, s1); break;
        case O_MAD:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) * (%s) + (%s)", s0, s1, s2); break;
        case O_LRP:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "mix((%s), (%s), (%s))", s2, s1, s0); break;
        case O_MIN:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "min((%s), (%s))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_MAX:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "max((%s), (%s))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_DP3:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(dot((%s).xyz, (%s).xyz))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_DP4:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(dot((%s), (%s)))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_DP2ADD: w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(dot((%s).xy, (%s).xy) + (%s).x)", s0, s1, s2); break;
        case O_RCP:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(1.0 / (%s).x, 3.402823466e+38, (%s).x == 0.0))", s0, s0); break;
        case O_RSQ:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(inverseSqrt(abs((%s).x)), 3.402823466e+38, abs((%s).x) == 0.0))", s0, s0); break;
        case O_FRC:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "fract(%s)", s0); break;
        case O_ABS:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "abs(%s)", s0); break;
        case O_CMP:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "select((%s), (%s), (%s) >= vec4f(0.0))", s2, s1, s0); break;
        case O_CND:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "select((%s), (%s), (%s) > vec4f(0.5))", s2, s1, s0); break;
        case O_POW:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(pow(abs((%s).x), (%s).x))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_NRM:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(normalize((%s).xyz), vec3f(0.0), length((%s).xyz) == 0.0), 1.0)", s0, s0); break;
        case O_EXP:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(exp2((%s).x))", s0); break;
        /* expp: (2^floor(x), fract(x), 2^x, 1) */
        case O_EXPP:   w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(exp2(floor((%s).x)), fract((%s).x), exp2((%s).x), 1.0)", s0, s0, s0); break;
        case O_LOGP:   w = snprintf(ex, WEX,
                           "vec4f(floor(log2(max(abs((%s).x), 1e-38))),"
                           " abs((%s).x) * exp2(-floor(log2(max(abs((%s).x), 1e-38)))),"
                           " log2(max(abs((%s).x), 1e-38)), 1.0)", s0, s0, s0, s0); break;
        case O_LOG:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(log2(abs((%s).x)), -3.4e+38, (%s).x == 0.0))", s0, s0); break;
        default:
            continue;                   /* unsupported: skipped, as on the Mac */
        }
        if (w < 0 || w >= WEX){ x.bad = 1; break; }
        if (!y->has_dst) continue;
        /* destination: same register map as the sources (msl_dst); anything
         * else would not compile on the Mac either -> reject */
        int dty = RT(y->dst);
        if (dty != R_TEMP && dty != R_INPUT && dty != R_ADDR && dty != R_COLOROUT){ x.bad = 1; break; }
        char d[64]; w_reg(&x, d, sizeof d, y->dst, 0);
        int sh = DSHIFT(y->dst);
        char k[48] = "";
        if (sh) w_float(k, sizeof k, ldexpf(1.f, sh));
        if (sh && SATUR(y->dst)) w = snprintf(val, WEX, "saturate((%s) * %s)", ex, k);
        else if (sh)             w = snprintf(val, WEX, "((%s) * %s)", ex, k);
        else if (SATUR(y->dst))  w = snprintf(val, WEX, "saturate(%s)", ex);
        else                     w = snprintf(val, WEX, "%s", ex);
        if (w < 0 || w >= WEX){ x.bad = 1; break; }
        w_store(&bb, d, WMASK(y->dst), val, 0);
        /* the headlight term (W_HL) */
        int dn = RN(y->dst);
        if (p->version < 0x0200 && dty == R_TEMP && (WMASK(y->dst) & 7u) == 7u && !sh && !SATUR(y->dst)){
            if (y->op == O_MUL && ((w_plain(y->src[0], R_ADDR, 1) && w_plain(y->src[1], R_ADDR, 2)) ||
                                   (w_plain(y->src[0], R_ADDR, 2) && w_plain(y->src[1], R_ADDR, 1)))){
                hl_mul = dn; continue; }
            if (y->op == O_MAD && dn == hl_mul && w_plain(y->src[0], R_TEMP, dn) && w_plain(y->src[1], R_CONST, 0)
                && (tcuse & 6u) == 6u){
                wb_put(&bb, "  r%d = vec4f(r%d.xyz + hl_more(i.uv1, tc2.y), r%d.w);\n", dn, dn, dn);
                hl_used = 1; hl_mul = -1; continue; }
        }
        if (dty == R_TEMP && dn == hl_mul) hl_mul = -1;
    }
    if (x.bad || !bb.ok) goto done;

    int usec = ps_uses_colorout(p);
    if (usec) x.oC = 1; else x.r |= 1u;          /* the result register */
    WBuf ob; wb_init(&ob, out, cap);
    wb_put(&ob, "// ps_%d: %s_%u_%u, %u instructions%s%s\n", id, "ps", p->version >> 8, p->version & 0xFF,
           p->n, (cubemask & 1u) ? ", stage 0 cube" : "", hl_used ? ", other cars' headlights" : "");
    wb_put(&ob, "%s%s", W_VOUT, W_PSPAR);
    w_textures(&ob, cubemask);
    if (hl_used) wb_put(&ob, "%s", W_HL);
    wb_put(&ob, "@fragment fn ps_%d(i: VOut) -> @location(0) vec4f {\n", id);
    w_decls(&ob, &x, 16);
    if (x.v & 1u) wb_put(&ob, "  var v0 = i.col0;\n");
    if (x.v & 2u) wb_put(&ob, "  var v1 = i.col1;\n");
    for (int t = 0; t < 4; t++) if (x.t & (1u << t)) wb_put(&ob, "  var t%d = vec4f(0.0);\n", t);
    if (x.oC) wb_put(&ob, "  var oC = vec4f(0.0);\n");
    wb_put(&ob, "%s", bodybuf);
    wb_put(&ob, "  return ps_end(%s, i.fog);\n}\n", usec ? "oC" : "r0");
    if (ob.ok) rc = (int)ob.n;
done:
    free(bodybuf); free(ex); free(s0); free(s1); free(s2); free(val);
    return rc;
}
int ps_to_wgsl_ex(const VSProg *p, int id, char *out, size_t cap, unsigned cubemask){
    return ps_to_wgsl_ex2(p, id, out, cap, cubemask, -1);
}
int ps_to_wgsl(const VSProg *p, int id, char *out, size_t cap){
    return ps_to_wgsl_ex(p, id, out, cap, 0u);
}

/* ====================================================================
 * Vertex shader (vs_to_msl)
 * ==================================================================== */

/* D3DDECLTYPE -> WGSL expression reading at byte address B + off.  Must match
 * com.c decl_fetch (the CPU path) bit for bit -- the Mac's decl_read_msl only
 * gets within an ulp, its divisions run under Metal fast math -- and reject
 * the same types, so the draw takes the CPU path. */
static int decl_read_wgsl(char *o, size_t cap, unsigned type, unsigned off){
    switch (type){
    case 0: snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(ldf(B + %uu), 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)",off); break;                       /* FLOAT1 */
    case 1: snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(ldf(B + %uu), ldf(B + %uu), 0.0, 1.0)",off,off+4); break;          /* FLOAT2 */
    case 2: snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(ldf(B + %uu), ldf(B + %uu), ldf(B + %uu), 1.0)",
                     off,off+4,off+8); break;                                                         /* FLOAT3 */
    case 3: snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(ldf(B + %uu), ldf(B + %uu), ldf(B + %uu), ldf(B + %uu))",
                     off,off+4,off+8,off+12); break;                                                  /* FLOAT4 */
    case 4: snprintf(o,cap,"ldcolor(B + %uu)",off); break;                                           /* D3DCOLOR */
    case 5: snprintf(o,cap,"ldub4(B + %uu)",off); break;                                             /* UBYTE4 */
    case 8: snprintf(o,cap,"n8(ldub4(B + %uu))",off); break;                                        /* UBYTE4N */
    case 6: snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu), 0.0, 1.0)",off,off+2); break;          /* SHORT2 */
    case 7: snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu))",
                     off,off+2,off+4,off+6); break;                                                   /* SHORT4 */
    case 9: snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(s16n(vec4f(lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu), 0.0, 0.0)).xy, 0.0, 1.0)",
                     off,off+2); break;                                                               /* SHORT2N */
    case 10:snprintf(o,cap,"s16n(vec4f(lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu), lds(B + %uu)))",
                     off,off+2,off+4,off+6); break;                                                   /* SHORT4N */
    case 11:snprintf(o,cap,"vec4f(u16n(vec4f(ldu(B + %uu), ldu(B + %uu), 0.0, 0.0)).xy, 0.0, 1.0)",
                     off,off+2); break;                                                               /* USHORT2N */
    case 12:snprintf(o,cap,"u16n(vec4f(ldu(B + %uu), ldu(B + %uu), ldu(B + %uu), ldu(B + %uu)))",
                     off,off+2,off+4,off+6); break;                                                   /* USHORT4N */
    default: return 0;
    }
    return 1;
}

/* Destination of a vertex shader write (vs_dst_msl): oT4..7 alias oT0..3 and
 * unknown registers go to a scratch variable, exactly as on the Mac. */
static int w_vsdst(WCtx *x, char *o, size_t cap, unsigned tok){
    int ty = RT(tok), n = RN(tok);
    switch (ty){
    case R_TEMP:    n &= 31; x->r |= 1u << n; snprintf(o, cap, "r%d", n); return 0;
    case R_ADDR:    x->a0 = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "a0"); return 1;
    case R_RASTOUT: if (n == 0){ snprintf(o, cap, "oPos"); return 0; }
                    if (n == 1){ snprintf(o, cap, "oFog"); return 0; }
                    x->dummy = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "dummy"); return 0;
    case R_ATTROUT: snprintf(o, cap, "oD%d", n & 1); return 0;
    case R_OUTPUT:  snprintf(o, cap, "oT%d", n & 3); return 0;
    default:        x->dummy = 1; snprintf(o, cap, "dummy"); return 0;
    }
}

int vs_to_wgsl(const VSProg *p, int id, const int decl[16][2], char *out, size_t cap){
    if (!p || !out || cap < 1024) return 0;
    if (!w_defs_finite(p)) return 0;
    WCtx x; memset(&x, 0, sizeof x); x.p = p; x.vs = 1;
    char *bodybuf = malloc(cap);
    if (!bodybuf) return 0;
    WBuf bb; wb_init(&bb, bodybuf, cap);
    char *ex = malloc(WEX), *s0 = malloc(WEX), *s1 = malloc(WEX), *s2 = malloc(WEX), *val = malloc(WEX);
    int rc = 0;
    if (!ex || !s0 || !s1 || !s2 || !val) goto done;

    /* inputs from the declaration (baked offsets and types) */
    unsigned vdecl = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++){
        if (decl[i][0] < 0) continue;
        char e[256];
        if (!decl_read_wgsl(e, sizeof e, (unsigned)decl[i][1], (unsigned)decl[i][0])) goto done;
        wb_put(&bb, "  let v%d = %s;\n", i, e);
        vdecl |= 1u << i;
    }

    for (unsigned q = 0; q < p->n && bb.ok && !x.bad; q++){
        const VSIns *y = &p->ins[q];
        if (y->nsrc > 0) w_src(&x, s0, WEX, y->src[0], y->rel[0]);
        if (y->nsrc > 1) w_src(&x, s1, WEX, y->src[1], y->rel[1]);
        if (y->nsrc > 2) w_src(&x, s2, WEX, y->src[2], y->rel[2]);
        int w = 0;
        ex[0] = 0;
        switch (y->op){
        case O_NOP: case O_DCL: case O_DEF: case O_DEFI: case O_DEFB:
        case O_LABEL: case O_END: continue;
        case O_MOV:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "%s", s0); break;
        case O_ADD:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) + (%s)", s0, s1); break;
        case O_SUB:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) - (%s)", s0, s1); break;
        case O_MUL:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) * (%s)", s0, s1); break;
        case O_MAD:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "(%s) * (%s) + (%s)", s0, s1, s2); break;
        case O_MIN:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "min((%s), (%s))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_MAX:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "max((%s), (%s))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_SLT:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "select(vec4f(0.0), vec4f(1.0), (%s) < (%s))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_SGE:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "select(vec4f(0.0), vec4f(1.0), (%s) >= (%s))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_DP3:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(dot((%s).xyz, (%s).xyz))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_DP4:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(dot((%s), (%s)))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_LRP:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "mix((%s), (%s), (%s))", s2, s1, s0); break;
        case O_FRC:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "fract(%s)", s0); break;
        case O_ABS:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "abs(%s)", s0); break;
        case O_RCP:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(1.0 / (%s).x, 3.402823466e+38, (%s).x == 0.0))", s0, s0); break;
        case O_RSQ:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(inverseSqrt(abs((%s).x)), 3.402823466e+38, abs((%s).x) == 0.0))", s0, s0); break;
        case O_EXP:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(exp2((%s).x))", s0); break;
        case O_EXPP: w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(exp2(floor((%s).x)), fract((%s).x), exp2((%s).x), 1.0)", s0, s0, s0); break;
        /* vertex logp is the one-component log on the Mac */
        case O_LOG: case O_LOGP:
                     w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(log2(abs((%s).x)), -3.4e+38, (%s).x == 0.0))", s0, s0); break;
        case O_POW:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(pow(abs((%s).x), (%s).x))", s0, s1); break;
        case O_CRS:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(cross((%s).xyz, (%s).xyz), 1.0)", s0, s1); break;
        case O_NRM:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(select(normalize((%s).xyz), vec3f(0.0), length((%s).xyz) == 0.0), 1.0)", s0, s0); break;
        case O_SGN:  w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "sign(%s)", s0); break;
        case O_M4x4: case O_M4x3: case O_M3x3: case O_M3x4: case O_M3x2: {
            /* m?x? dst, src0, src1: rows are consecutive registers from src1
             * (as on the Mac: K.c rows ignore def and relative addressing) */
            int rows = (y->op==O_M4x4) ? 4 : (y->op==O_M4x3 ? 3 :
                       (y->op==O_M3x3 ? 3 : (y->op==O_M3x4 ? 4 : 2)));
            int vec3 = (y->op==O_M3x3 || y->op==O_M3x4 || y->op==O_M3x2);
            const char *sw2 = vec3 ? ".xyz" : "";
            WBuf eb; wb_init(&eb, ex, WEX);
            wb_put(&eb, "vec4f(");
            for (int rr = 0; rr < rows; rr++){
                unsigned tok2 = y->src[1];
                int ty2 = RT(tok2), nn2 = RN(tok2) + rr;
                if (ty2 == R_CONST2) nn2 += 2048; else if (ty2 == R_CONST3) nn2 += 4096;
                else if (ty2 == R_CONST4) nn2 += 6144;
                char row[48];
                if (ty2 == R_TEMP){ x.r |= 1u << (nn2 & 31); snprintf(row, sizeof row, "r%d", nn2 & 31); }
                else if (ty2 == R_INPUT){ x.v |= 1u << (nn2 & 15); snprintf(row, sizeof row, "v%d", nn2 & 15); }
                else snprintf(row, sizeof row, "K.c[kb + %du]", (nn2 & 255) + 1);
                wb_put(&eb, "%sdot((%s)%s, (%s)%s)", rr ? ", " : "", s0, sw2, row, sw2);
            }
            for (int rr = rows; rr < 4; rr++) wb_put(&eb, ", %s", rr == 3 ? "1.0" : "0.0");
            wb_put(&eb, ")");
            w = eb.ok ? (int)eb.n : -1;
            break; }
        case O_SINCOS: w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(cos((%s).x), sin((%s).x), 0.0, 0.0)", s0, s0); break;
        case O_MOVA:   w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "%s", s0); break;
        case O_LIT:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX,
                           "vec4f(1.0, max((%s).x, 0.0), select(0.0, pow(max((%s).y, 0.0),"
                           " clamp((%s).w, -127.9, 127.9)), (%s).x > 0.0), 1.0)", s0, s0, s0, s0); break;
        case O_DST:    w = snprintf(ex, WEX, "vec4f(1.0, (%s).y * (%s).y, (%s).z, (%s).w)", s0, s1, s0, s1); break;
        default:
            /* flow control, calls, ...: rejected, the draw keeps the CPU path */
            goto done;
        }
        if (w < 0 || w >= WEX){ x.bad = 1; break; }
        if (!y->has_dst) continue;
        if (y->op == O_MOVA){
            /* MSL round() rounds half away from zero; WGSL round() is
             * half-to-even, so spell the Mac's rounding out.  The mask is
             * ignored as on the Mac. */
            x.a0 = 1;
            wb_put(&bb, "  { let e = %s; a0 = vec4i(sign(e) * floor(abs(e) + 0.5)); }\n", ex);
            continue;
        }
        char d[64]; int toint = w_vsdst(&x, d, sizeof d, y->dst);
        if (SATUR(y->dst)) w = snprintf(val, WEX, "saturate(%s)", ex);
        else               w = snprintf(val, WEX, "%s", ex);
        if (w < 0 || w >= WEX){ x.bad = 1; break; }
        /* a0 writes: float -> int truncates toward zero, as the Mac's MSL
         * implicit conversion */
        w_store(&bb, d, WMASK(y->dst), val, toint);
    }
    if (x.bad || !bb.ok) goto done;

    WBuf ob; wb_init(&ob, out, cap);
    wb_put(&ob, "// vs_%d: vs_%u_%u, %u instructions, vs_kmax %d\n", id, p->version >> 8, p->version & 0xFF,
           p->n, vs_kmax(p));
    wb_put(&ob, "%s%s%s%s", W_VOUT, W_VSPAR, W_PULL, W_TPICK);
    wb_put(&ob, "@vertex fn vs_%d(@builtin(vertex_index) vid: u32, @builtin(instance_index) iid: u32) -> VOut {\n", id);
    /* kb <= GW_KWIN_ROWS - 257 (the renderer's window choice): every row
     * below, relative addressing's clamp included, stays inside the window */
    wb_put(&ob, "  let kb = iid;\n"
                "  let KH = bitcast<vec4u>(K.c[kb]);\n"
                "  let B = KH.z + vid * KH.x;\n");
    w_decls(&ob, &x, 32);
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
        if ((x.v & (1u << i)) && !(vdecl & (1u << i)))
            wb_put(&ob, "  let v%d = vec4f(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);\n", i);
    /* oFog defaults to 1 = no fog when the shader does not write it */
    wb_put(&ob, "  var oPos = vec4f(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);\n"
                "  var oD0 = vec4f(1.0); var oD1 = vec4f(0.0);\n"
                "  var oT0 = vec4f(0.0); var oT1 = vec4f(0.0); var oT2 = vec4f(0.0); var oT3 = vec4f(0.0);\n"
                "  var oFog = vec4f(1.0);\n");
    wb_put(&ob, "%s", bodybuf);
    /* Epilogue: D3D9's pixel centres, no colour clamp; D3DTSS_TEXCOORDINDEX
     * applied here so the pixel stage reads plain interpolants.
     * D3D9 samples pixel x at x, WebGPU at x + 0.5: the picture moves half a
     * pixel right and down (KH.w: the target's width | height << 16, 0 = as
     * it is; gpu_web.c target_wh), so the game's post passes, which add half
     * a texel to their UVs, read texel centres again (without it, half a
     * texel down and right, and the last row and column at 1.0). */
    wb_put(&ob, "  var o: VOut;\n"
                "  let ts = max(vec2f(f32(KH.w & 0xFFFFu), f32(KH.w >> 16u)), vec2f(1.0));\n"
                "  o.pos = vec4f(oPos.xy + select(vec2f(0.0), vec2f(1.0, -1.0) / ts, KH.w != 0u) * oPos.w, oPos.zw);\n"
                "  o.col0 = oD0; o.col1 = oD1;\n"
                "  o.uv0 = tpick(KH.y & 3u, oT0, oT1, oT2, oT3);\n"
                "  o.uv1 = tpick((KH.y >> 8u) & 3u, oT0, oT1, oT2, oT3);\n"
                "  o.uv2 = tpick((KH.y >> 16u) & 3u, oT0, oT1, oT2, oT3);\n"
                "  o.uv3 = tpick((KH.y >> 24u) & 3u, oT0, oT1, oT2, oT3);\n"
                "  o.fog = oFog.x;\n"
                "  return o;\n}\n");
    if (ob.ok) rc = (int)ob.n;
done:
    free(bodybuf); free(ex); free(s0); free(s1); free(s2); free(val);
    return rc;
}

/* ====================================================================
 * TVert vertex stage and fixed-function pixel stage (metal.m kShaderSrc:
 * vmain / fmain / fmain_nd).  Same ABI as the game shaders.
 * ==================================================================== */
int wgsl_tvert_module(char *out, size_t cap){
    WBuf ob; wb_init(&ob, out, cap);
    wb_put(&ob, "// vs_0: TVert pass-through (CPU-transformed vertices, metal.m vmain)\n");
    wb_put(&ob, "%s%s", W_VOUT, W_VSPAR);
    /* TVert (gfx.h): pos xyzw, oD0, oD1, t[4][4]: 28 f32 = 112 bytes.  The
     * renderer draws with firstVertex = MDraw.first from the start of the
     * TVert arena: no K block. */
    wb_put(&ob, "fn ld4(w: u32) -> vec4f { return bitcast<vec4f>(vec4u(VB[w], VB[w + 1u], VB[w + 2u], VB[w + 3u])); }\n");
    wb_put(&ob, "@vertex fn vs_0(@builtin(vertex_index) vid: u32) -> VOut {\n"
                "  let w = vid * 28u;\n"
                "  var o: VOut;\n"
                "  o.pos = ld4(w);\n"
                "  o.col0 = ld4(w + 4u); o.col1 = ld4(w + 8u);\n"
                "  o.uv0 = ld4(w + 12u); o.uv1 = ld4(w + 16u); o.uv2 = ld4(w + 20u); o.uv3 = ld4(w + 24u);\n"
                "  o.fog = 1.0;\n"
                "  return o;\n}\n");
    return ob.ok ? (int)ob.n : 0;
}

int wgsl_ff_module(int id, char *out, size_t cap, unsigned cubemask){
    WBuf ob; wb_init(&ob, out, cap);
    int cube = cubemask & 1u;
    wb_put(&ob, "// ps_%d: fixed-function fragment col0 * tex0 (metal.m fmain)%s\n", id, cube ? ", stage 0 cube" : "");
    wb_put(&ob, "%s%s", W_VOUT, W_PSPAR);
    w_textures(&ob, cubemask);
    wb_put(&ob, "@fragment fn ps_%d(i: VOut) -> @location(0) vec4f {\n"
                "  return ps_end(i.col0 * textureSample(tex0, smp0, i.uv0.%s), i.fog);\n}\n",
           id, cube ? "xyz" : "xy");
    return ob.ok ? (int)ob.n : 0;
}

/* Compute module for the vertex-pulling test (web/src/test/shadercheck.ts):
 * for every supported declaration type t (0..12) and byte offset o (0..7) it
 * writes OUT[t * 8 + o] = decode(t, PT.base + o) with the same helpers and the
 * same decl_read_wgsl() text the vertex shaders use. */
int wgsl_pull_test_module(char *out, size_t cap){
    WBuf ob; wb_init(&ob, out, cap);
    wb_put(&ob, "// vertex-pulling test: OUT[type * 8 + offset] = decode(type, PT.x + offset)\n");
    wb_put(&ob, "@group(0) @binding(0) var<storage, read> VB: array<u32>;\n"
                "@group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read_write> OUT: array<vec4f>;\n"
                "@group(0) @binding(2) var<uniform> PT: vec4u;\n");
    wb_put(&ob, "%s", W_PULL);
    wb_put(&ob, "@compute @workgroup_size(1) fn main() {\n  let B = PT.x;\n");
    for (unsigned t = 0; t <= 12; t++)
        for (unsigned o = 0; o < 8; o++){
            char e[256];
            if (decl_read_wgsl(e, sizeof e, t, o)) wb_put(&ob, "  OUT[%u] = %s;\n", t * 8 + o, e);
        }
    wb_put(&ob, "}\n");
    return ob.ok ? (int)ob.n : 0;
}

/* whine.c -- each local player's gearbox whine, as ropi's Underground 2
 * Transmission Whine has it (UG2WhineGen 1.0.2: NFS Carbon's BMW M3 GTR
 * gearbox whine on Underground 2; source https://github.com/ropi336/UG2WhineGen,
 * "No Rights Reserved").  gearbox_whine = on (NFSU2_GEARBOX_WHINE=1); off by
 * default, the original game: nothing of the game read, nothing loaded,
 * nothing mixed.
 *
 * The mod's sounds are not in the game build: tools/whinepack.py puts the
 * three of its 1.0.2 release in the game folder's MODPACKS/WHINE (16-bit mono
 * WAVs), and the server serves them with the rest of the game.  With the
 * switch on they are read on a thread of their own at the first frame (so
 * only then fetched), and the mixer plays nothing until they are in.  A game
 * folder without them: no whine, and one line in the log.  Each looped from
 * the start over the game's sound:
 *   car_whine.wav          the whine, its pitch rising with the speed
 *   car_whine_2.wav        a second layer at its own pitch, louder with speed
 *   car_whine_reverse.wav  in reverse instead of both
 * What the mod does every 1/60 s (its ProcessWhine thread), here every frame
 * on the game thread with its per-tick steps scaled by the frame's time, for
 * each local player (split screen's 2 to 4, co-op's 2: split_render_limit)
 * a whine of its own:
 *   - the player's car: [PlayersByNumber[i] + 4] (this build keeps the
 *     player table at SPLIT_PLAYERS_INDEX); its speed +0x430 (m/s, times 3.6:
 *     km/h; the engine sound's) and its gear +0x434 (0 reverse, 1 neutral,
 *     2 first ..);
 *   - nothing unless the game is in the world (GameFlowManager [0x8654A4]
 *     6); silent while the world stands (paused, a menu over it, photo mode:
 *     the frame's world step [0x865154] 0), as the mod is while paused;
 *   - the level: the game's Master times Engine Volume (0x83AA28 +0 and
 *     +0x14), reached over about 12 ticks (the mod's fadeSnd), times LEVEL;
 *   - under 1 km/h the whine at pitch 0.3 and the rest silent; else the
 *     whine and reverse layer at 0.3 + 0.7 km/h / 330 + min(0.5
 *     sqrt(km/h / 70), 0.6) + m, m creeping 0.001 a tick towards 0.02 (gear
 *     - 1) as the car speeds up (down while it slows), the second layer at 1;
 *   - volumes: the whine 0.030, the second layer 0.015 km/h / 140, both off
 *     in reverse; the reverse layer 0.050 there only; all times the level;
 *   - an upshift: the whine and the second layer fade out over 0.1 s and
 *     stay silent 0.2 s more (the mod waits on, while the clutch is in, up
 *     to half a second; here the 0.3 s alone), and m jumps to its new gear's
 *     value.
 * Not here: the mod's car list (CarList: the whine on every car, as its
 * default ALL), its Volume (LEVEL instead), its F1 switch and its chimes
 * (the page's setting instead), and its lowering to 0.4 during a phone call
 * or cutscene.
 *
 * LEVEL: the mod plays its sounds through an audio engine of its own beside
 * the game's, both at full scale into the system's mix; the mixers here play
 * the game's sound buffers at their DirectSound volumes and nothing more
 * (audio_web.c, audio.m), so the mod's own gains keep its balance against
 * the game: the whine 11 to 13 dB under the engine alone while driving, lost
 * under it at speed.  Here it plays at 165 % of that.  Measured in a quick
 * race at 60 fps with every volume but Master and Engine at 0
 * (tests/scripts/whine_engine.txt, SNDDUMP): the whine about -32 dBFS (its
 * gains, its sounds' level and LEVEL; on minus off within 1 dB of that at
 * the start line), the engine alone -24 to -27 dBFS while driving and -22
 * at the line: the whine about 8 dB under the engine up to 90 km/h, 5 to 6
 * dB at 90 to 120 km/h, 10 dB at the line.  Its peak is at most 0.11 of
 * full scale (330 km/h), so it brings no clipping of its own: in a race with
 * every volume at 100 % the game's own sound reaches full scale without it.
 *
 * Threads: the game thread writes the targets, one word each; the mixer
 * smooths every change (so a word of the frame before beside one of this
 * frame is harmless), snaps each to its target once within a hair of it (no
 * denormals in a voice left to fade forever), and falls silent when they are
 * older than STALE_MS (a parked game). */
#include "whine.h"
#include "cpu.h"
#include "game.h"
#include "splitscreen_mem.h"
#include "setting.h"
#include <math.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <strings.h>
#include <time.h>

int fileio_mod_pack(const char *rel, char *out, size_t outsz);   /* fileio.c: MODPACKS/<rel>'s host path */

#define STALE_MS   250u
#define SEATS      4                  /* local players with a whine of their own (split screen has at most 4) */
#define LEVEL      1.65f              /* 165 % of the mod's Volume (above: why, and measured) */
#define MAX_BYTES  (4u << 20)         /* a sound file bigger than this is not the mod's */

/* ---- the mod's sounds: MODPACKS/WHINE (tools/whinepack.py) ----------------------------- */
typedef struct { const uint8_t *pcm; uint32_t n; float rate; } Wav;
enum { W_WHINE, W_WHINE2, W_REVERSE, W_N };
static const char *const k_file[W_N] = { "WHINE/car_whine.wav", "WHINE/car_whine_2.wav", "WHINE/car_whine_reverse.wav" };

static uint32_t rd16(const uint8_t *p){ return (uint32_t)p[0] | (uint32_t)p[1] << 8; }
static uint32_t rd32(const uint8_t *p){ return rd16(p) | rd16(p + 2) << 16; }
/* a 16-bit mono PCM WAV's samples; n 0 when it is not one */
static Wav wav_parse(const uint8_t *b, uint32_t len){
    Wav w = { 0, 0, 0.f };
    if (len < 12 || memcmp(b, "RIFF", 4) || memcmp(b + 8, "WAVE", 4)) return w;
    uint32_t rate = 0, fmt_ok = 0;
    for (uint32_t o = 12; o + 8 <= len;){
        uint32_t sz = rd32(b + o + 4);
        if (sz > len - o - 8) sz = len - o - 8;
        if (!memcmp(b + o, "fmt ", 4) && sz >= 16)
            fmt_ok = rd16(b + o + 8) == 1 && rd16(b + o + 10) == 1 && rd16(b + o + 22) == 16, rate = rd32(b + o + 12);
        else if (!memcmp(b + o, "data", 4) && fmt_ok && rate){
            w.pcm = b + o + 8; w.n = sz / 2; w.rate = (float)rate;
            return w;
        }
        o += 8 + sz + (sz & 1u);
    }
    return w;
}
static Wav g_wav[W_N];
static uint8_t *g_file[W_N];
static char g_path[W_N][1100];
static int g_ready;                   /* 0 not read (yet), 1 read, -1 none (the mixer adds nothing); atomic */
static inline float wav_s(const Wav *w, uint32_t i){ return (float)(int16_t)rd16(w->pcm + 2u * i) * (1.f / 32768.f); }

static uint32_t now_ms(void){
    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return (uint32_t)((uint64_t)ts.tv_sec * 1000u + (uint64_t)ts.tv_nsec / 1000000u);
}

/* the loader thread: the three files whole (on the web the page fetches them now) */
static void *load_main(void *arg){
    (void)arg;
    uint32_t t0 = now_ms(), bytes = 0; double secs = 0;
    int ok = 1;
    for (int w = 0; w < W_N && ok; w++){
        FILE *f = fopen(g_path[w], "rb");
        long len = -1;
        if (f && !fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END) && (len = ftell(f)) > 44 && (uint32_t)len <= MAX_BYTES && !fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET) &&
            (g_file[w] = malloc((size_t)len)) && fread(g_file[w], 1, (size_t)len, f) == (size_t)len)
            g_wav[w] = wav_parse(g_file[w], (uint32_t)len);
        if (f) fclose(f);
        if (g_wav[w].n < 4){ fprintf(stderr, "[whine] MODPACKS/%s is not a sound this reads: no whine\n", k_file[w]); ok = 0; }
        else { bytes += (uint32_t)len; secs += (double)g_wav[w].n / g_wav[w].rate; }
    }
    if (!ok){
        for (int w = 0; w < W_N; w++){ free(g_file[w]); g_file[w] = 0; g_wav[w].n = 0; }
        __atomic_store_n(&g_ready, -1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        return 0;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "[whine] the mod's sounds: %d (%.1f s, %u KB) in %u ms\n", W_N, secs, bytes >> 10, now_ms() - t0);
    __atomic_store_n(&g_ready, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
    return 0;
}

/* ---- game thread -> mixer: one word per field ----------------------------------------- */
static uint32_t fbits(float f){ uint32_t u; memcpy(&u, &f, 4); return u; }
static float bitsf(uint32_t u){ float f; memcpy(&f, &u, 4); return f; }
#define GET(f)    __atomic_load_n(&(f), __ATOMIC_RELAXED)
#define PUT(f, v) __atomic_store_n(&(f), (v), __ATOMIC_RELAXED)
static struct { uint32_t gain, pitch; } g_in[SEATS][W_N];
static uint32_t g_stamp, g_level;     /* the targets' time (ms); the level (Master x Engine, 0 paused) */
static int g_on = -1;                 /* the setting (game thread) */

static void whine_init(void){
    if (g_on >= 0) return;
    g_on = setting_bool("NFSU2_GEARBOX_WHINE", 0);
    if (!g_on) return;
    int have = 1;
    for (int w = 0; w < W_N; w++) have = have && fileio_mod_pack(k_file[w], g_path[w], sizeof g_path[w]);
    if (!have){
        fprintf(stderr, "[whine] gearbox whine on, but the game folder has no MODPACKS/WHINE (tools/whinepack.py): no whine\n");
        __atomic_store_n(&g_ready, -1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
        return;
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "[whine] gearbox whine on: reading its sounds\n");
    pthread_t t; pthread_attr_t a; pthread_attr_init(&a); pthread_attr_setdetachstate(&a, PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED);
    if (pthread_create(&t, &a, load_main, 0)) load_main(0);
    pthread_attr_destroy(&a);
}

/* one of the game's volumes (G_VOLUMES + off), 1 while it is not there or not one */
static float game_volume(uint32_t off){
    uint32_t a = G_VOLUMES + off;
    if (!mem_is_committed(a) || !mem_is_committed(a + 3u)) return 1.f;
    float v = MRF32(a);
    return v >= 0.f && v <= 1.f ? v : 1.f;
}

/* a local player's car, 0 for none */
static uint32_t seat_car(int s){
    uint32_t a = SPLIT_PLAYERS_INDEX + 4u * (uint32_t)s;
    uint32_t pl = mem_is_committed(a + 3u) ? MR32(a) : 0u;
    uint32_t car = pl && mem_is_committed(pl + 7u) ? MR32(pl + 4u) : 0u;
    return car && mem_is_committed(car + CAR_GEAR + 3u) ? car : 0u;
}

/* a player's whine state, as the mod's: its car, the gear before (0: none yet, as its gGearOld), the pitch's gear part
 * (m), the speed before and the upshift's silence left */
typedef struct { uint32_t car; int32_t gear_old; float mod, speed_last, shift; } Seat;
static Seat g_seat[SEATS];

static void put(int s, int w, float gain, float pitch){ PUT(g_in[s][w].gain, fbits(gain)); PUT(g_in[s][w].pitch, fbits(pitch)); }
static void seat_quiet(int s){
    g_seat[s] = (Seat){ 0 };
    for (int w = 0; w < W_N; w++) PUT(g_in[s][w].gain, fbits(0.f));
}

static void seat_step(int s, uint32_t car, float dt){
    Seat *S = &g_seat[s];
    if (car != S->car){
        *S = (Seat){ .car = car };
        fprintf(stderr, "[whine] player %d's car 0x%08x: its whine\n", s + 1, car);
    }
    float kmh = MRF32(car + CAR_SPEED) * 3.6f;
    int32_t gear = (int32_t)MR32(car + CAR_GEAR);
    if (!isfinite(kmh)) kmh = 0.f;
    int play = gear != 0;                                /* not in reverse */
    float ticks = dt * 60.f;                             /* the mod's 1/60 s steps in this frame */

    float pitch = 0.3f, pitch2 = 1.f;
    if (kmh < 1.f){
        pitch2 = 0.f;
    } else {
        float target = (float)(gear - 1) * 0.020f;
        if (target < 0.f) target = 0.f;
        /* the mod's gearJustChanged: an upshift, not the first gear seen */
        int up = S->gear_old != 0 && gear > S->gear_old;
        if (S->gear_old == 0 || gear != S->gear_old) S->gear_old = gear;
        if (up){ S->shift = 0.3f; S->mod = target; }
        if (S->speed_last > kmh && S->mod > target){ S->mod -= 0.001f * ticks; if (S->mod < target) S->mod = target; }
        if (S->speed_last < kmh && S->mod < target){ S->mod += 0.001f * ticks; if (S->mod > target) S->mod = target; }
        S->speed_last = kmh;
        float m = 0.5f * sqrtf(kmh / 70.f);
        pitch = 0.3f + kmh / 330.f * 0.7f + (m > 0.6f ? 0.6f : m) + S->mod;
    }
    float shifting = 1.f;
    if (S->shift > 0.f){ S->shift -= dt; shifting = 0.f; }
    float g1 = 0.030f * (float)play * shifting;
    float g2 = (kmh > 0.f ? kmh / 140.f : 0.f) * 0.015f * (float)play * shifting;
    float gr = 0.050f * (float)!play;
    put(s, W_WHINE, g1, pitch);
    put(s, W_WHINE2, kmh < 1.f ? 0.f : g2, pitch2);
    put(s, W_REVERSE, kmh < 1.f ? 0.f : gr, pitch);
}

void whine_frame(void){
    whine_init();
    if (!g_on || __atomic_load_n(&g_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) < 0) return;
    int flow6 = mem_is_committed(G_FLOW + 3u) && MR32(G_FLOW) == 6u;
    float dt = flow6 ? MRF32(G_WORLDDT) : 0.f;
    int run = flow6 && dt > 0.f && dt < 0.25f;
    int n = split_render_limit();
    if (n < 1) n = 1;
    if (n > SEATS) n = SEATS;
    PUT(g_stamp, now_ms());
    PUT(g_level, fbits(run ? game_volume(0x00u) * game_volume(0x14u) * LEVEL : 0.f));
    for (int s = 0; s < SEATS; s++){
        uint32_t car = flow6 && s < n ? seat_car(s) : 0u;
        if (!car){ if (g_seat[s].car || !flow6) seat_quiet(s); continue; }
        if (run) seat_step(s, car, dt);                  /* the world standing: as it was, silent by the level */
    }
}

/* ---- mixer thread ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
static struct { double pos; float gain, pitch; } g_v[SEATS][W_N];
static float g_lvl;

/* x one step of one-pole smoothing (k) towards t, and t itself once within a hair of it */
static inline float glide(float x, float t, float k){
    x += (t - x) * k;
    return fabsf(t - x) < 1e-6f ? t : x;
}

void whine_mix(float *acc, unsigned frames, unsigned rate){
    if (!rate || !frames || __atomic_load_n(&g_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != 1) return;
    float fs = (float)rate;
    int stale = now_ms() - GET(g_stamp) > STALE_MS;
    /* the level as the mod's fadeSnd (about 12 ticks), the gains over 0.1 s as its fade on an upshift, the pitch
     * over 20 ms; all as one-pole smoothing, each sample */
    float k_lvl = 1.f - expf(-1.f / (0.070f * fs)), k_gain = 1.f - expf(-1.f / (0.035f * fs)), k_pitch = 1.f - expf(-1.f / (0.020f * fs));
    float lvl_t = stale ? 0.f : bitsf(GET(g_level));
    if (!(lvl_t >= 0.f && lvl_t <= 4.f)) lvl_t = 0.f;
    if (g_lvl == 0.f && lvl_t == 0.f) return;            /* silent, and staying so: the voices keep their place */
    float gt[SEATS][W_N], pt[SEATS][W_N];
    int live[SEATS * W_N], nl = 0;
    for (int s = 0; s < SEATS; s++) for (int w = 0; w < W_N; w++){
        gt[s][w] = bitsf(GET(g_in[s][w].gain)); pt[s][w] = bitsf(GET(g_in[s][w].pitch));
        if (!(gt[s][w] >= 0.f && gt[s][w] < 1.f)) gt[s][w] = 0.f;
        if (!(pt[s][w] >= 0.f && pt[s][w] < 4.f)) pt[s][w] = 0.f;
        if (gt[s][w] > 0.f || g_v[s][w].gain > 0.f) live[nl++] = s * W_N + w;   /* the rest: silent, and staying so */
    }
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < frames; i++){
        g_lvl = glide(g_lvl, lvl_t, k_lvl);
        float out = 0.f;
        for (int j = 0; j < nl; j++){
            int s = live[j] / W_N, w = live[j] % W_N;
            const Wav *W = &g_wav[w];
            float g = g_v[s][w].gain = glide(g_v[s][w].gain, gt[s][w], k_gain);
            float p = g_v[s][w].pitch = glide(g_v[s][w].pitch, pt[s][w], k_pitch);
            double pos = g_v[s][w].pos;
            uint32_t i0 = (uint32_t)pos, i1 = i0 + 1u >= W->n ? 0u : i0 + 1u;
            float t = (float)(pos - (double)i0), a = wav_s(W, i0);
            out += (a + (wav_s(W, i1) - a) * t) * g;
            pos += (double)(p * W->rate / fs);
            if (pos >= (double)W->n) pos = fmod(pos, (double)W->n);
            g_v[s][w].pos = pos;
        }
        out *= g_lvl;
        acc[2u * i] += out; acc[2u * i + 1u] += out;
    }
}

/* whine.h -- each local player's gearbox whine, as ropi's Underground 2

#ifndef WHINE_H

/* widescreen.c - native-resolution presentation on screens wider (or
 * narrower) than the game's own 4:3 mode.
 *
 * The game keeps rendering for the mode it picked (1280x960, 640x480 HUD
 * space); com.c creates the device at the window's backing pixels and maps
 * the 4:3 HUD into the middle of the screen (res_pick / aspect_apply).  That
 * mapping alone leaves a few things wrong, which the hooks here fix at the
 * game's own code sites (the ones ThirteenAG's NFSUnderground2.WidescreenFix
 * patches, MIT; addresses verified in our SPEED2.EXE v1.2):
 *
 *   FOV       Hor+ in the projection setup (sub_005c7ec0) for the views that
 *             fill the screen.  The old renderer-side Hor+ scaled every
 *             perspective draw, including the car's cube map faces, and the
 *             game still culled with its 4:3 frustum.
 *   borders   the cutscene letterbox bars are 640-unit HUD quads and covered
 *             only the 4:3 middle of the screen.
 *   FMV       movie quad extents (fit / fill / stretch).
 *   HUD       optional edge anchoring of the race HUD (WFP's .dat table).
 *   marker    a HUD marker placed over a world position (sub_004ebec0)
 *             gets the inverse of the HUD squeeze.
 *   rain      the lens rain drops keep their 4:3 shape.
 *   fill      quads over a whole render target (sub_005c7140: the rain and
 *             overcast tint) are 640-unit HUD quads too and covered only the
 *             4:3 middle; the renderer leaves them full size.
 *
 *   shape     optional square pixels in the views that fill the screen: the
 *             game's projection makes the picture 4-14 % too wide (below).
 *
 * Every hook site is listed with HOOK_SITE() so gen.sh can hand it to the
 * lifter (fill is an override of the whole function).  Options (all read once):
 *   NFSU2_FOV=game|renderer       where Hor+ is applied (default game)
 *   NFSU2_FOV_SCALE=original|correct  the game's proportions (default) or
 *                                 square pixels (WidescreenFix's "FOV Scale:
 *                                 Mathematically Correct")
 *   NFSU2_HUD=43|wide             centred 4:3 HUD or edge-anchored HUD
 *   NFSU2_MOVIE=fit|fill|stretch  FMV framing (default fit = pillarbox)
 *   NFSU2_CUTSCENE_BORDERS=full|off  letterbox bars across the whole width
 *                                    (default) or none
 *   NFSU2_RENDER=backing|panel|scale:<f>  device size of the "native" display
 *                                 row: the window's backing pixels (default),
 *                                 the physical panel's pixel density, or the
 *                                 backing size times f                     */
#include "widescreen.h"
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

enum { FOV_GAME, FOV_RENDERER };
enum { HUD_43, HUD_WIDE };
enum { MOV_FIT, MOV_FILL, MOV_STRETCH };
enum { BRD_FULL, BRD_OFF };
enum { RENDER_BACKING, RENDER_PANEL, RENDER_SCALE };
enum { SHAPE_ORIGINAL, SHAPE_CORRECT };

static int   g_init;
static int   g_fov = FOV_GAME, g_hud = HUD_WIDE, g_movie = MOV_FIT, g_brd = BRD_FULL;
static int   g_shape = SHAPE_ORIGINAL;
static int   g_hudfix = 1;
static int   g_render = RENDER_BACKING;
static double g_render_f = 1.0;
static float g_k = 1.f;                 /* game aspect / device aspect */
static unsigned long g_hits[16];
/* FE re-render after a mapping change (see the 0x52c711 hook): until this
 * many frames are drawn, at most g_redirty_cap more objects. */
static long g_redirty_until;
static unsigned g_redirty_cap;

static int opt_is(const char *v, const char *s){ return v && !strcasecmp(v, s); }
static void ws_init(void){
    if (g_init) return;
    g_init = 1;
    const char *e;
    if ((e = getenv("NFSU2_FOV")) && *e)
        g_fov = opt_is(e, "renderer") ? FOV_RENDERER : FOV_GAME;
    if ((e = getenv("NFSU2_HUD")) && *e)
        g_hud = (opt_is(e, "43") || opt_is(e, "4:3")) ? HUD_43 : HUD_WIDE;
    if ((e = getenv("NFSU2_MOVIE")) && *e)
        g_movie = opt_is(e, "fill") ? MOV_FILL : opt_is(e, "stretch") ? MOV_STRETCH : MOV_FIT;
    if ((e = getenv("NFSU2_CUTSCENE_BORDERS")) && *e)
        g_brd = (opt_is(e, "off") || *e == '0') ? BRD_OFF : BRD_FULL;
    if ((e = getenv("NFSU2_FOV_SCALE")) && *e)
        g_shape = (opt_is(e, "correct") || opt_is(e, "corrected")) ? SHAPE_CORRECT : SHAPE_ORIGINAL;
    /* HUDFIX=0: legacy, HUD stretched to the full width (diagnostic). */
    if ((e = getenv("HUDFIX")) && *e == '0') g_hudfix = 0;
    if ((e = getenv("NFSU2_RENDER")) && *e){
        if (opt_is(e, "panel")) g_render = RENDER_PANEL;
        else if (!strncasecmp(e, "scale:", 6) || (*e >= '0' && *e <= '9') || *e == '.'){
            double f = atof(strchr(e, ':') ? strchr(e, ':') + 1 : e);
            if (f >= 0.25 && f <= 2.0){ g_render = RENDER_SCALE; g_render_f = f; }
            else fprintf(stderr, "ws: NFSU2_RENDER=%s ignored (scale 0.25..2)\n", e);
        }
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "ws: fov=%s fov scale=%s hud=%s movie=%s cutscene borders=%s render=%s",
            g_fov == FOV_GAME ? "game" : "renderer", g_shape == SHAPE_CORRECT ? "correct" : "original",
            g_hud == HUD_WIDE ? "wide" : "4:3",
            g_movie == MOV_FIT ? "fit" : g_movie == MOV_FILL ? "fill" : "stretch",
            g_brd == BRD_FULL ? "full" : "off",
            g_render == RENDER_PANEL ? "panel" : g_render == RENDER_SCALE ? "scale" : "backing");
    if (g_render == RENDER_SCALE) fprintf(stderr, ":%.3g", g_render_f);
    fprintf(stderr, "\n");
}

/* Device size of the "native" display row relative to the window's backing
 * pixels (com.c modes_refresh).  panel: the physical panel's density, which
 * in a scaled display mode is lower than the backing store's (3024 panel
 * pixels for 3600 backing pixels on this Mac); never above the backing
 * store, the window server would only scale it down again. */
double ws_render_factor(void){
    ws_init();
    double f = 1.0;
    if (g_render == RENDER_PANEL){
        double bs = 0.0, pp = 0.0;
        void metal_screen_metrics(double *, double *);
        metal_screen_metrics(&bs, &pp);
        if (bs > 0.0 && pp > 0.0) f = pp / bs;
        if (f > 1.0) f = 1.0;
    } else if (g_render == RENDER_SCALE) f = g_render_f;
    return f;
}

double ws_max_pixels(void){
    const char *e = getenv("NFSMAXPIX");
    return (e && *e) ? atof(e) : WS_MAX_PIXELS_DEFAULT;
}

void ws_set_mapping(float k){
    ws_init();
    if (!(k > 0.05f && k < 20.f)) k = 1.f;
    if (k != g_k){
        long metal_frames(void);
        fprintf(stderr, "ws: game/device aspect %.4f\n", (double)k);
        g_redirty_until = metal_frames() + 3; g_redirty_cap = 100000;
    }
    g_k = k;
}
/* The test script's "fovscale MODE" (autotest.c), for an A/B in one run. */
int ws_set_fov_scale(const char *mode){
    ws_init();
    if (opt_is(mode, "original")) g_shape = SHAPE_ORIGINAL;
    else if (opt_is(mode, "correct") || opt_is(mode, "corrected")) g_shape = SHAPE_CORRECT;
    else return 0;
    return 1;
}
float ws_persp_x(void){ ws_init(); return g_fov == FOV_RENDERER ? fminf(g_k, 1.f) : 1.f; }
float ws_persp_y(void){ ws_init(); return g_fov == FOV_RENDERER ? fminf(1.f / g_k, 1.f) : 1.f; }
float ws_ui_x(void){ ws_init(); return g_hudfix ? fminf(g_k, 1.f) : 1.f; }
float ws_ui_y(void){ ws_init(); return g_hudfix ? fminf(1.f / g_k, 1.f) : 1.f; }

/* HUD space is 640x480 and com.c shows it in the middle of the screen; the
 * whole screen is 640/ui_x units wide.  Extra units on each side: */
static float hud_extra_x(void){ return 320.f * (1.f / ws_ui_x() - 1.f); }
static float hud_extra_y(void){ return 240.f * (1.f / ws_ui_y() - 1.f); }

/* ---- edge-anchored HUD ---------------------------------------------------
 * Element anchors from WidescreenFix's NFSUnderground2.WidescreenFix.dat
 * (73 entries, identical to the copy in the user's install): FE object
 * position (x, y) -> anchored to the left (-1) or right (+1) screen edge.
 * WFP shifts by -109/+119 units at 16:9, i.e. 2.33 resp. 12.33 units more
 * than the 106.67 extra units a 16:9 screen has.  Here the shift is the
 * extra width the screen really has plus that margin; the margin fades in
 * up to 16:9, so a 4:3 window gets no shift and 16:9 matches WFP exactly.
 * Wider than 16:9 the HUD stays on the edges of a centred 16:9 area: the
 * game stops drawing some backing panels (tachometer dial, leaderboard box)
 * once they lie entirely beyond its 640-unit screen, which happened from
 * about 2.2:1 on (21:9 test). */
static const struct { int16_t x, y; int8_t side; } g_anchor[] = {
    {-295,-170,-1},{-295,-186,-1},{-295,-204,-1},{-295,-211,-1},       /* EA Trax text */
    {-173,-177,-1},{-127,-177,-1},{-275,-181,-1},{-125,-177,-1},       /* EA Trax */
    { -31,-177,-1},{-131,-177,-1},{ -42,-177,-1},{-275,-182,-1},
    { -43,-177,-1},{ -92,-177,-1},{ -93,-177,-1},{  33,-177,-1},
    {-223,  70,-1},{-223, 142,-1},{-223,  71,-1},{-223, 143,-1},       /* minimap */
    {-143, 196,-1},
    {-248,-122,-1},{-195,-112,-1},                                     /* SMS bar, icon */
    {-185, -66,-1},{-196,-185,-1},{-224,-117,-1},                      /* drift info */
    { 142, 195, 1},{ 199, 177, 1},{-110, -26,-1},{-254, 171,-1},       /* tachometer */
    { 205, 181, 1},{ 168, 202, 1},{ 207, 175, 1},{ 160, 206, 1},
    { 220, 151, 1},{ 253, 117, 1},                                     /* N2O */
    {-263,  36,-1},                                                    /* satellite signal */
    { 285,  14, 1},                                                    /* "too slow" */
    { 270,  91, 1},{ 284,  -9, 1},{ 284,  -2, 1},{ 295, -89, 1},       /* N2O earned */
    { 295, -78, 1},
    {-246,-158,-1},{ 224,-157, 1},                                     /* outrun distance, time */
    { 257,-182, 1},{ 213,-224, 1},{ 196,-100, 1},{ 215,-159, 1},       /* leaderboard */
    { 224, -52, 1},{ 253,-149, 1},{ 217,-161, 1},{ 240,-161, 1},
    { 139,-163, 1},{ 223, -52, 1},{ 266,-180, 1},{ 280,-129, 1},
    { 275,-167, 1},{ 187,-190, 1},{ 179,-134, 1},{ 242,-161, 1},
    { 219,-161, 1},{ 140,-162, 1},{ 223, -52, 1},{ 224,-132, 1},
    { 191,-127, 1},{ 201,-137, 1},                                     /* test run module */
    { 227,-184, 1},{ 193,-194, 1},{ 283,-163, 1},                      /* bank */
    {-223,  34,-1},{-223, -87,-1},{-223,-172,-1},                      /* wrong way sign */
};
/* x offset for the element anchored at (x, y); 0 if it is not anchored. */
static float hud_shift(float x, float y){
    if (g_hud != HUD_WIDE) return 0.f;
    float extra = hud_extra_x();
    if (extra <= 0.f) return 0.f;
    int ix = (int)floorf(x), iy = (int)floorf(y);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof g_anchor / sizeof g_anchor[0]; i++){
        if (g_anchor[i].x != ix || g_anchor[i].y != iy) continue;
        const float e169 = 320.f * (16.f / 9.f * 0.75f - 1.f);          /* 106.67 */
        float m = (g_anchor[i].side < 0 ? 109.f : 119.f) - e169;        /* 2.33 / 12.33 */
        float e = fminf(extra, e169);
        float d = e + m * e / e169;
        return g_anchor[i].side < 0 ? -d : d;
    }
    return 0.f;
}

/* the edge anchoring's x shift for an element at (x, y) (0: not one of the anchored places); splitscreen.c */
float ws_hud_shift(float x, float y){ return hud_shift(x, y); }

static uint32_t fbits(float f){ uint32_t u; memcpy(&u, &f, 4); return u; }
static float    bitsf(uint32_t u){ float f; memcpy(&f, &u, 4); return f; }

/* Cutscene letterbox bar: four (x, y, z, w) vertices in 640x480 HUD units,
 * passed to the quad drawer sub_005c5020.  The game draws them from x 0 to
 * 640, i.e. only across the 4:3 middle of a wider screen. */
static int g_border_quad;
int ws_take_border_quad(void){ int b = g_border_quad; g_border_quad = 0; return b; }
static void border_quad(uint32_t v){
    if (!v || !mem_is_committed(v) || !mem_is_committed(v + 63u)) return;
    g_border_quad = 1;
    float ex = hud_extra_x() + 1.f, ey = hud_extra_y() + 1.f;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++){
        uint32_t a = v + 16u * (uint32_t)i;
        float x = MRF32(a), y = MRF32(a + 4u);
        if (g_brd == BRD_OFF){ MRF32(a) = 0.f; continue; }      /* zero width, like WFP */
        MRF32(a) = x < 320.f ? -ex : 640.f + ex;
        /* Narrower than 4:3: the picture extends above and below the HUD
         * space, keep the bars on its outer edges. */
        if (y <= 0.f) MRF32(a + 4u) = -ey; else if (y >= 480.f) MRF32(a + 4u) = 480.f + ey;
    }
}

/* FMV quad (sub_00536950 -> sub_0051a1c0): left, top, right, bottom in HUD
 * fractions, -0.5..0.5 = the 4:3 HUD space.  Fit leaves it (pillarbox on a
 * wide screen), fill covers the screen keeping the aspect, stretch fills
 * the screen ignoring it. */
static void movie_quad(uint32_t sp){
    float sx = 1.f / ws_ui_x(), sy = 1.f / ws_ui_y();          /* screen in HUD units */
    float hx = 0.5f, hy = 0.5f;
    if (g_movie == MOV_FILL){ float s = fmaxf(sx, sy); hx = hy = 0.5f * s; }
    else if (g_movie == MOV_STRETCH){ hx = 0.5f * sx; hy = 0.5f * sy; }
    if (fabsf(MRF32(sp) + 0.5f) > 1e-4f || fabsf(MRF32(sp + 8u) - 0.5f) > 1e-4f) return;
    MRF32(sp) = -hx; MRF32(sp + 4u) = -hy; MRF32(sp + 8u) = hx; MRF32(sp + 12u) = hy;
}

/* sub_005c7140(surface, texture, colour, ?, src blend, dest blend, flag)
 * makes the surface the render target and draws one quad over all of it:
 * 0..640 x 0..480 HUD units, i.e. identity-matrix clip space, which com.c
 * narrows to the 4:3 middle like the HUD.  Its callers mean the whole
 * target: sub_005c7860's weather tint (DESTCOLOR x SRCCOLOR, a 16x16 grey
 * texture times the rain/overcast colour, into the frame's copy) and two
 * alpha passes in sub_005caad0.  While it runs, aspect_apply leaves
 * orthographic draws alone. */
static int g_fill;
void sub_005c7140_orig(CPU *c);
void sub_005c7140(CPU *c){
    g_hits[12]++;
    g_fill++;
    sub_005c7140_orig(c);
    g_fill--;
}
int ws_fill_target(void){ return g_fill > 0; }

void ws_hud_marker(float *x, float *y){
    ws_init();
    if (g_fov != FOV_GAME) return;
    float ux = ws_ui_x(), uy = ws_ui_y();
    if (ux < 1.f) *x = 320.f + (*x - 320.f) / ux;
    if (uy < 1.f) *y = 240.f + (*y - 240.f) / uy;
}

int ws_hook(CPU *c, uint32_t ip){
    ws_init();
    switch (ip){
    /* sub_005c7ec0, projection setup per eView ([ebp+4] = view id):
     *   P00 = 1/tan(FOV*hscale/2) stored at 0x5c7fee,
     *   P11 = 1/tan(FOV*aspect/2) stored at 0x5c8025,
     * then the view*projection product and the culling frustum planes are
     * built from them.  Views 1/2 (player) and 4/5 (their road reflection,
     * projected in screen space) fill the screen and get Hor+ (or Vert+ on
     * a narrower screen).  The rear-view mirror (3), shadow views (9, 10)
     * and the cube map faces (16-21) keep the game's projection.
     *
     * Shape: in those views hscale = [0x7a27dc] = 1.1 and aspect = the view's
     * H/W (960/1280) x [0x7a27e0] / [0x7a27d8] = 1.1 / 0.8696, so the angle
     * is scaled, not its tangent, and pixels are not square: a wheel shows
     * 1.14 times as wide as tall at the garage's ~32 degrees, 1.09-1.11 at
     * the race cameras' 65-75.  NFSU2_FOV_SCALE=correct keeps the game's
     * height (P11, after any Vert+) and makes P00 = P11 x the device's H/W
     * (= the view's H/W x k): the picture shows 4-14 % more at the sides.  At
     * 0x5c8025 P00 waits at [esp+0x28] (stored after 0x5c7fee, three pushes
     * ago) and goes into the matrix after; the product and the culling
     * planes are made of both, so they agree. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x005c7fee):
    case HOOK_SITE(0x005c8025): {
        g_hits[ip == 0x005c7feeu ? 0 : 1]++;
        if (g_fov != FOV_GAME) return 1;
        uint32_t view = mem_is_committed(c->ebp + 4u) ? MR32(c->ebp + 4u) : 0u;
        if (!(view == 1u || view == 2u || view == 4u || view == 5u)) return 1;
        double before = ST(0);
        uint32_t vp = mem_is_committed(c->ebp + 0x5bu) ? MR32(c->ebp + 0x58u) : 0u;
        uint32_t vw = vp && mem_is_committed(vp + 0x1bu) ? MR32(vp + 0x14u) : 0u;
        uint32_t vh = vp && mem_is_committed(vp + 0x1bu) ? MR32(vp + 0x18u) : 0u;
        if (ip == 0x005c7feeu){ if (g_k < 1.f) ST(0) *= (double)g_k; }
        else if (g_k > 1.f) ST(0) /= (double)g_k;
        { static unsigned shown[2]; int s = ip == 0x005c7feeu ? 0 : 1;
          if (shown[s] < 4 && ST(0) != before){ shown[s]++;
              fprintf(stderr, "ws: view %u %s %.4f -> %.4f (view size %ux%u)\n", view,
                      s ? "P11" : "P00", before, ST(0), vw, vh); } }
        if (ip == 0x005c8025u && g_shape == SHAPE_CORRECT && vw && vh
            && mem_is_committed(c->esp + 0x2bu)){
            float p00 = MRF32(c->esp + 0x28u);
            float sq = (float)(ST(0) * (double)vh / (double)vw * (double)g_k);
            if (p00 > 0.01f && p00 < 100.f && sq > 0.01f && sq < 100.f){
                MRF32(c->esp + 0x28u) = sq; g_hits[13]++;
                static unsigned said;
                if (said < 4 && fabsf(sq - p00) > 1e-4f){ said++;
                    fprintf(stderr, "ws: view %u square pixels: P00 %.4f -> %.4f (P11 %.4f, k %.4f)\n",
                            view, (double)p00, (double)sq, ST(0), (double)g_k); }
            }
        }
        return 1; }
    /* sub_004ebec0 puts a HUD marker over a world position: the view's
     * screen position (sub_005bc4a0, from the view*projection product, so
     * already Hor+) divided by the view size, times 640 resp. 480 HUD
     * units.  The HUD is shown narrowed to the 4:3 middle, so the marker
     * needs the inverse of that (it sat k times too close to the centre). */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x004ec35c):
    case HOOK_SITE(0x004ec36e): {
        int y = ip == 0x004ec36eu;
        g_hits[y ? 9 : 8]++;
        if (g_fov != FOV_GAME) return 1;
        float u = y ? ws_ui_y() : ws_ui_x(), c0 = y ? 240.f : 320.f;
        if (u < 1.f) ST(0) = c0 + (ST(0) - c0) / u;
        return 1; }
    /* Rain drops on the lens (sub_005c7b..): quads in clip units, centre
     * [esp+10] plus/minus the extent in ST0 (= [esp+0c]).  The same extent
     * in x and y gave 4:3-shaped drops at 4:3 and wider ones on a wider
     * screen; scaling x by the HUD factor keeps the original shape (WFP W2
     * makes them round and smaller instead). */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x005c7ce9): {
        g_hits[10]++;
        ST(0) *= (double)ws_ui_x();
        return 1; }
    /* Letterbox bars: top (0x5cbebd) and bottom (0x5cbf31) quad, the vertex
     * pointer is the first argument already on the stack. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x005cbebd):
    case HOOK_SITE(0x005cbf31):
        g_hits[2]++;
        border_quad(MR32(c->esp));
        return 1;
    /* FMV quad: the four extents are the last four pushes. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x00536a32):
        g_hits[3]++;
        movie_quad(c->esp);
        return 1;
    /* Edge-anchored HUD, the four places WidescreenFix hooks:
     * FE object position just stored to [esp+60]/[esp+64]. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x0051b198): {
        g_hits[4]++;
        float x = MRF32(c->esp + 0x60u), y = MRF32(c->esp + 0x64u);
        float d = hud_shift(x, y);
        if (d != 0.f) MRF32(c->esp + 0x60u) = x + d;
        return 1; }
    /* Radar blips: ecx = [ebx+1c] is about to be stored as the blip x. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x0051d655): {
        g_hits[5]++;
        float x = bitsf(c->ecx), y = MRF32(c->ebx + 0x20u);
        float d = hud_shift(x, y);
        if (d != 0.f) c->ecx = fbits(x + d);
        return 1; }
    /* ecx = [esi+1c], stored as the element x a few instructions later. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x004c6759): {
        g_hits[6]++;
        float x = bitsf(c->ecx), y = MRF32(c->esi + 0x20u);
        float d = hud_shift(x, y);
        if (d != 0.f) c->ecx = fbits(x + d);
        return 1; }
    /* "Stop sign": [esi] = ST0 + [edx] was just stored; move it by the
     * shift of the anchor at [edx]. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x0050516f): {
        g_hits[7]++;
        float d = hud_shift(MRF32(c->edx), MRF32(c->edx + 4u));
        if (d != 0.f) MRF32(c->esi) += d;
        return 1; }
    /* FEng's render traversal (sub_0052c5d0), edi = the child about to be
     * drawn.  FEng rebuilds an object's vertices only when its flags (+1c)
     * have 0x400000 set, which its own setters do when they move it.  The
     * HUD anchoring above is applied while the vertices are built, so
     * after a resize or a fullscreen switch in a race the static parts
     * (tachometer dial, minimap ring, leaderboard labels) kept the old
     * shift while needles and numbers followed.  For a few frames after
     * the mapping changes every object drawn gets that flag. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x0052c711): {
        long metal_frames(void);
        if (g_redirty_cap && metal_frames() < g_redirty_until){
            g_redirty_cap--; g_hits[11]++;
            if (mem_is_committed(c->edi + 0x1fu)) MR32(c->edi + 0x1cu) |= 0x400000u;
        }
        return 1; }
    /* The same for a package's top-level objects: the package loop
     * (sub_00536520) draws them itself, ebx = the object about to be drawn
     * (a group goes to the traversal above).  The race leaderboard's header
     * panel is one: turned from portrait to landscape in a race, it stayed
     * where the portrait screen had it. */
    case HOOK_SITE(0x00536745): {
        long metal_frames(void);
        void menusize_obj(CPU *);
        menusize_obj(c);
        if (g_redirty_cap && metal_frames() < g_redirty_until){
            g_redirty_cap--; g_hits[11]++;
            if (mem_is_committed(c->ebx + 0x1fu)) MR32(c->ebx + 0x1cu) |= 0x400000u;
        }
        return 1; }
    default:
        return 0;
    }
}

void ws_report(void){
    if (!g_init) return;
    fprintf(stderr, "ws: hooks fov=%lu/%lu borders=%lu movie=%lu hud=%lu/%lu/%lu/%lu marker=%lu/%lu rain=%lu"
            " fe-rerender=%lu fill=%lu square=%lu (k=%.4f)\n",
            g_hits[0], g_hits[1], g_hits[2], g_hits[3],
            g_hits[4], g_hits[5], g_hits[6], g_hits[7], g_hits[8], g_hits[9], g_hits[10],
            g_hits[11], g_hits[12], g_hits[13], (double)g_k);
}

/* Stage 3 seed: the Win32 API subset needed to boot + tracing for the rest. */
#include <stdatomic.h>

#include <time.h>

#include <unistd.h>

#include "setting.h"      /* ENVC: getenv once per call site (per-draw paths) */

jmp_buf g_exit_jmp;
int g_exit_code = 0;
int g_exit_armed = 0;

typedef struct { uint32_t iat; const char*dll; const char*name; int nargs; } ImpEnt;
extern const ImpEnt g_imp[]; extern const uint32_t g_imp_count;
/* One import index space for SPEED2.EXE and the lifted DLLs (module.c):
